truths.truth: cargo build --locked at the repo root produces an executable named cadence and cargo test --locked passes, with Cargo.lock committed and target/ ignored
truths.evidence: `./target/debug/cadence --version` -> `cadence 3.7.12`, exit 0. `cargo test --locked` -> 6 passed (unit) + 4 passed (tests/mcp.rs), 0 failed. `git ls-files Cargo.lock` lists it; .gitignore:60 carries `target/`; `git status --porcelain` shows only the untracked UAT.md.

truths.truth: A build from an empty target directory succeeds with --locked and the resulting binary completes an initialize + tools/list handshake and exits 0 on stdin close
truths.evidence: CARGO_TARGET_DIR=<scratch> cargo build --locked --offline -> exit 0, 101 crates compiled from scratch including tree-sitter 0.27.0, tree-sitter-md/json/python/javascript/rust, rmcp 3.2.0, rmcp-macros, grep-searcher. The freshly built binary answered serverInfo {"name":"cadence","version":"3.7.12"} and tools/list ["cadence_version"], and `: | cadence serve` exited 0. Caveat: RUSTC_WRAPPER is set on this machine (compile cache), so the 11.59s wall time is not a cold-compiler figure; the repo's own target/ was deliberately not `cargo clean`ed, since deleting it is a mutation the verifier does not make.

truths.truth: cadence serve names the server `cadence` and declares exactly one tool, cadence_version, carrying an outputSchema
truths.evidence: Spawned `./target/debug/cadence serve` over stdio: initialize -> serverInfo {"name":"cadence","version":"3.7.12"}; tools/list -> 1 tool, `cadence_version`, outputSchema keys ['$defs','$schema','oneOf']. Source: crates/cadence/src/server.rs:73 `#[tool_handler(name = "cadence")]`, :48-56 the single `#[tool]`.

truths.truth: A tool call returns the typed envelope as structured content on a successful call - status ok, isError not true - and the same four tags reach the wire schema
truths.evidence: tools/call cadence_version -> isError false, structuredContent {"status":"ok","version":"3.7.12","os":"linux","arch":"x86_64"}, plus a mirrored text block. The declared outputSchema's oneOf branches carry status consts ['ok','refused','unknown','not-applicable'] - the hyphen survives to the wire, not just to the unit test. crates/cadence/src/server.rs:56-70 returns `Json<Envelope<VersionReport>>`.

truths.truth: The envelope is one serde-tagged enum whose four tags serialize exactly, and a refused envelope through rmcp's structured-output path is a successful call (D-07)
truths.evidence: crates/cadence/src/envelope.rs:41 `#[serde(tag = "status", rename_all = "kebab-case")]`, :59 explicit `rename = "not-applicable"`. Named test `envelope::tests::refused_is_a_successful_call_carrying_its_refusal` (envelope.rs:152-176) runs `Json(envelope).into_call_tool_result()` and asserts structured_content["status"] == "refused" and is_error != Some(true); it passes. No `CallToolResult::error` or `structured_error` anywhere in the crate.

truths.truth: .github/workflows/test.yml carries a job that builds and tests the crate with --locked beside the untouched Node matrix
truths.evidence: yaml parse -> jobs ['cargo-test','node-test','self-verify','typecheck']. test.yml:65-92 installs the channel rust-toolchain.toml names, then `cargo build --locked` and `cargo test --locked`. `git diff 290536c9~7 HEAD -- .github/workflows/test.yml` is 29 insertions, 0 deletions, so nothing existing was replaced. truths.evidence: yaml parse -> jobs ['build','guard','publish'], on = ['push','workflow_dispatch'], jobs.build.needs = 'guard', fail-fast false, targets exactly aarch64-apple-darwin / aarch64-unknown-linux-musl / x86_64-apple-darwin / x86_64-unknown-linux-musl. release.yml:44 gates the reachability step on `github.event_name == 'push'` while the test and self-verify steps run on both events. Every `uses:` in both workflows carries a 40-hex SHA (checkout, setup-node, upload-artifact@043fb46d). 112 insertions, 0 deletions across the phase, so the publish job is byte-unchanged.

truths.truth: package.sh produces a byte-reproducible two-entry archive and prints one sha256sum-format line that sha256sum -c accepts
truths.evidence: Ran .github/scripts/package.sh twice on the same stand-in binary with the file's mtime changed (touch -t 202001010000 then 202606061212) and umask changed (022 then 077) between runs: identical line a13b185a...bed89, and `cmp` reports the two .tar.gz files byte-identical. `tar tvzf` lists exactly <name>/cadence (0755, uid/gid 0, mtime epoch) and <name>/LICENSE (0644). `sha256sum -c` on the printed line reports OK.
